correctness.rationale: Every nonalgebraic type is an admissible ideal/filter pair (L,U) over a finite named poset, giving t(P)=2i(P)-1+m(P). For a chosen maximal x and Q=P\{x}, its strict predecessors D form an ideal; the incomparable subposet H=Q\D yields i(P)=i(Q)+i(H) and j(P)=j(Q)+|H|. Since i(H)>=|H|+1, induction gives i(P)>=n+1+j(P). Each comparable a<b gives a distinct mixed type (downarrow a, uparrow b), so m(P)>=c(P), yielding t(P)>=binom(n+2,2)+j(P) and exact nonnegative two-term defect. Nonchain connected comparability components contain an incomparable distance-two pair sharing a neighbor; their union downset/upset gives an additional mixed type not associated with a comparable pair. For disjoint k chains, i(P)=prod(n_i+1), j=e2 and m=c, so defect=2 sum_{r>=3}e_r and equality iff k<=2 (including empty poset). A fresh independent exhaustive enumeration for all labeled posets n=0..4 matched both the inequality and exact equality classification.
